stats.label: Win %
stats.what: Regular-season winning percentage.

stats.label: Net rating
stats.what: Points scored minus points allowed per 100 possessions in his games.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Luck-adjusted net
stats.what: Net rating with opponents' 3P% and FT% set to league average, the same adjustment the Teams tab makes.
stats.formula: Net + 100 × (3 × (opp 3PM − opp 3PA × lg 3P%) + (opp FTM − opp FTA × lg FT%)) ÷ possessions

stats.label: Wins above talent
stats.what: Wins per 82 games beyond what his roster's prior-season impact predicted, before he touched it.
stats.formula: Actual wins − expected wins; expected from the talent line (expect.py), fitted out of sample
stats.source: the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card); the model in expect.py

stats.label: Wins above the market
stats.what: Wins per 82 beyond the preseason win total the sportsbooks posted for his team.
stats.source: Basketball-Reference preseason odds pages (each season's page is the source)
stats.sample: Hatched under 82 games; blank where no win total was posted.

stats.label: Wins above the spread
stats.what: Wins beyond what the closing spreads implied, game by game, added up (football Coaching Savant's method).
stats.formula: Σ (won − P(win | closing spread)); P from the league's empirical curve
stats.sample: Hatched under 82 games with a line.

stats.label: Against the spread
stats.what: How often his teams covered the closing spread.
stats.sample: Hatched under 82 games with a line.

stats.label: Close-game win %
stats.what: Winning percentage in games decided by five or fewer. Mostly luck, which is why it is shown next to point differential.

stats.label: Playoff rate
stats.what: Share of his full seasons that reached the playoffs.

stats.label: Rotation stability
stats.what: Share of scripted player-minutes that went to script: each man on or off the floor in the minutes his usual windows say.
stats.sample: Hatched under 41 games. The model's view, not a verdict: it cannot see fatigue, minor injuries, match-ups or development plans.

stats.label: Chosen deviation
stats.what: Off-script minutes with no absence, blowout or foul trouble to explain them: match-ups, benchings, hot hands, experiments.
stats.sample: Hatched under 41 games. The model's view, not a verdict: it cannot see fatigue, minor injuries, match-ups or development plans.

stats.label: Shake-up after a loss
stats.what: How much more off-script the rotation runs in the game after a loss than after a win, in percentage points.
stats.formula: Mean off-script share after losses − after wins

stats.label: Rides the hot hand
stats.what: Extra fourth-quarter minutes for a man 8+ points over his average through three quarters, against the minutes his usual windows give him. A tendency.
stats.formula: Mean (Q4 minutes − usual Q4 minutes) on hot nights

stats.label: Depth
stats.what: Players averaging 10+ minutes, per game.
stats.formula: Mean count of men with 10+ minutes

stats.label: Top-five minutes share
stats.what: Share of the team's minutes played by its five most-used men each game. Concentration.
stats.formula: Mean per game of top-5 minutes ÷ 240

stats.label: Starters' minutes
stats.what: Minutes per game to the five starters, added up.

stats.label: Stint length
stats.what: Average length of a continuous spell on the floor, in minutes.

stats.label: First substitution
stats.what: How long into the game the first substitution comes, in minutes.
stats.formula: Mean seconds to the first substitution ÷ 60

stats.label: All-bench minutes
stats.what: Minutes per game with no starter on the floor.
stats.formula: Mean seconds with zero starters on ÷ 60

stats.label: Closing-five talent gap
stats.what: In close games (within 10 at the buzzer, no garbage time): how far the five on the floor at the end sat below the best five available by impact, in points per 100. Lower is better; zero means he closed with his best five.
stats.formula: Mean over close games of (Σ BPM of the top five available − Σ BPM of the closing five)
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card)
stats.sample: Hatched under 15 close games. The model's view, not a verdict: it cannot see fatigue, minor injuries, match-ups or development plans.

stats.label: Closes with four of his best five
stats.what: Share of close games where at least four of the closing five were among the best five available by impact.
stats.formula: Games with 4+ of the top five on the floor at the buzzer ÷ close games
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card)
stats.sample: Hatched under 15 close games. The model's view, not a verdict: it cannot see fatigue, minor injuries, match-ups or development plans.

stats.label: Overplayed minutes
stats.what: Minutes per game above the league's fair-minutes line for the impact involved, summed over the men above it. Lower is better.
stats.formula: Σ max(0, MPG − fair MPG(BPM)) over the roster; the fair line is the league's minutes-by-impact fit that season
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card)
stats.sample: Hatched under 41 games. The model's view, not a verdict: it cannot see fatigue, minor injuries, match-ups or development plans.

stats.label: Minutes to 23-and-under
stats.what: Share of the team's minutes played by men 23 and under.
stats.formula: Σ minutes of players aged ≤ 23.5 ÷ team minutes
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card) ages

stats.label: Rookies' minutes
stats.what: Share of minutes played by rookies.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card)

stats.label: Sits an early second foul
stats.what: Minutes a man sits after his second foul in the first quarter.
stats.formula: Mean seconds from the foul to his return ÷ 60

stats.label: Staggers his top two
stats.what: Share of minutes with exactly one of his two most-used men on the floor.
stats.formula: Seconds with one of the two on ÷ seconds

stats.label: Lineups left on the table
stats.what: Minutes per game to five-man units projected two or more points per 100 below the team's best available arrangement. Lower is better.
stats.formula: Σ minutes of units with projected net ≤ best − 2 ÷ games (units.py / modules.fit_parts)
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card)
stats.sample: Hatched under 41 games. The model's view, not a verdict: it cannot see fatigue, minor injuries, match-ups or development plans.

stats.label: Timeouts per game
stats.what: Full and 20-second timeouts he called, per game.

stats.label: Timeouts during runs
stats.what: Share of his timeouts called while the opponent was on a 6-0 run or better.

stats.label: Timeouts left over
stats.what: Full timeouts unused at the end of games decided by five or fewer. Lower is better.
stats.formula: Mean (allowed − used) in close finishes; 7 allowed from 2017-18, 8 before

stats.label: Stops runs
stats.what: Opponent points per possession over the five possessions after his timeout during a run, against the league's figure for the same runs with no timeout. Negative is good: the run cooled more than runs cool on their own.
stats.formula: (opp PPP after his run timeouts − league opp PPP after matched runs without one), matched on run size

stats.label: After-timeout offense
stats.what: Points per possession on the first possession after his timeout when his team had the ball.
stats.formula: Σ points ÷ possessions, first possession after his timeouts, own ball

stats.label: ATO over his half-court
stats.what: After-timeout points per possession minus his team's ordinary half-court figure (possessions starting from a dead ball or a made basket).

stats.label: Late-game ATO
stats.what: After-timeout points per possession in the last two minutes of the fourth and overtime.

stats.label: After-timeout defense
stats.what: Opponent points per possession on the first possession after his timeout when the opponent had the ball. Lower is better.

stats.label: Halftime adjustment
stats.what: Third-quarter net rating minus first-half net rating, averaged over games, against the league's typical change.
stats.formula: Mean (Q3 net − H1 net) − league mean

stats.label: Challenges per game
stats.what: Coach's challenges per game.

stats.label: Challenge success
stats.what: Share of his challenges that overturned the call.

stats.label: Challenges saved for the fourth
stats.what: Share of his challenges used in the fourth quarter or overtime.

stats.label: Fouls up three
stats.what: With a three-point lead and 24 seconds or less, how often his defense fouled before a shot.
stats.formula: Possessions fouled ÷ possessions up 3 with ≤ 24 s

stats.label: Two-for-one
stats.what: Possessions per game ended by a shot with 28 to 40 seconds left in a quarter, the two-for-one window.

stats.label: End-of-quarter possessions
stats.what: Points per possession on possessions starting with 24 seconds or less in a quarter (regulation).

stats.label: Chases with fouls
stats.what: Trailing by 2 to 10 in the last two minutes: share of opponent possessions his defense fouled before a shot.

stats.label: Timeouts to advance
stats.what: Late-game timeouts called with the ball, tied or trailing, within three seconds of gaining it: advancing the ball. Per game.

stats.label: Clutch net rating
stats.what: Net rating in the last five minutes within five. Mostly noise; shown next to his overall net.
stats.formula: 100 × (pts − opp pts) ÷ possessions in clutch time

stats.label: Pace
stats.what: Possessions per 48 minutes.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Seconds per possession
stats.what: Average length of his team's possessions.

stats.label: Early offense
stats.what: Share of possessions over within seven seconds.

stats.label: Transition shots
stats.what: Share of field-goal attempts within seven seconds of a steal or defensive rebound.

stats.label: 3-point rate
stats.what: Share of shots from three.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Rim rate
stats.what: Share of shots in the restricted area.

stats.label: Mid-range rate
stats.what: Share of shots that are long twos.

stats.label: Corner-3 share
stats.what: Share of threes from the corners.

stats.label: Free-throw rate
stats.what: Free-throw attempts per field-goal attempt.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Assisted share
stats.what: Share of made baskets that were assisted.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Turnover rate
stats.what: Turnovers per 100 possessions. Lower is better.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Offensive rebounding
stats.what: Share of his team's misses it rebounded. Crash or get back.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Offensive rating
stats.what: Points per 100 possessions.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Passes per 100
stats.what: Passes made per 100 possessions.

stats.label: Seconds per touch
stats.what: How long the ball sits in one man's hands.
stats.formula: The NBA's average seconds per touch

stats.label: Drives per 100
stats.what: Drives to the basket per 100 possessions.

stats.label: Pull-up share
stats.what: Of jump shots, the share taken off the dribble rather than off the catch.

stats.label: Screen assists per 100
stats.what: Screens that led directly to a made basket, per 100 possessions.

stats.label: Hub touches per 100
stats.what: Elbow, post and paint touches per 100 possessions: an inside-out offense.

stats.label: Offensive box outs per 100
stats.what: Box outs on the offensive glass per 100 possessions.

stats.label: Defensive rating
stats.what: Points allowed per 100 possessions. Lower is better.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Opponent 3-point rate
stats.what: Share of opponents' shots from three. What he lets them have.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Opponent rim rate
stats.what: Share of opponents' shots in the restricted area.

stats.label: Opponent mid-range rate
stats.what: Share of opponents' shots that are long twos: the shot a defense wants to give.

stats.label: Opponent free-throw rate
stats.what: Opponents' free-throw attempts per shot. Lower is better.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Forced turnovers
stats.what: Opponent turnovers per 100 possessions.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Steals per 100
stats.what: Steals per 100 opponent possessions.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Deflections per 100
stats.what: Deflections per 100 opponent possessions. Disruption.

stats.label: Charges per 100
stats.what: Charges drawn per 100 possessions.

stats.label: Defensive rebounding
stats.what: Share of opponents' misses his team rebounded.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Transition allowed
stats.what: Share of opponents' shots within seven seconds of a steal or defensive rebound. Lower is better.

stats.label: Fouls per 100
stats.what: Personal fouls committed per 100 opponent possessions.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Switches per 100
stats.what: Switches per 100 matchup possessions, the closest public stand-in for a switch-everything scheme. A season is counted over the games its defensive box scores cover.
stats.formula: 100 × Σ switchesOn ÷ Σ partial matchup possessions (BoxScoreDefensiveV2, one per game)
stats.source: NBA.com matchup data (defensive box scores), 2017-18 on
stats.sample: Hatched under 41 games with a box score.

stats.label: Opponent eFG%
stats.what: Opponents' effective field-goal percentage. Lower is better.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the NBA's team tables before

stats.label: Beats the aging curve
stats.what: Change in his players' impact from the season before, against what the aging curve expects at their ages, minutes-weighted: in percentile points of position-adjusted BPM, the currency the curve was fitted on.
stats.formula: Σ w × (Δ BPM percentile − expected Δ(age)) ÷ Σ w, w = min(minutes both seasons); players with 500+ minutes both seasons and the same position bucket
stats.source: the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card); the aging curve in savant_config.AGING
stats.sample: Hatched under 2,000 weighted minutes. Selection, team staff and regression to the mean all live in this number.

stats.label: Young players beat the curve
stats.what: The same, for players 24 and under.
stats.source: the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card)

stats.label: Against the top ten
stats.what: Net rating against opponents in the top ten by luck-adjusted net as of the game date, minus his overall net.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; NBA game logs (stats.nba.com), 1996-97 on

stats.label: On a back-to-back
stats.what: Net rating on the second night of a back-to-back minus his overall net.

stats.label: On the road
stats.what: Net rating away minus net at home.

stats.label: Without regulars
stats.what: Net rating with five or more points of regular impact missing, minus his net at full strength.
stats.source: ESPN play-by-play, 2002-03 on; the Basketball Savant player archive (BPM as on each player's card)

stats.label: Trailing at the half
stats.what: Second-half margin, in points, in games his team trailed at the half.
stats.formula: Mean (Q3 + Q4 margin) when behind at the half

stats.label: Tempo control
stats.what: Where the game's pace landed between the two teams' usual paces: 100 means his pace, 0 the opponent's.
stats.formula: Mean (game pace − opp usual) ÷ (own usual − opp usual), seasons' prior games only

stats.label: As the favourite
stats.what: Margin against the spread when favoured minus when the underdog.

tables.games: One row per team-game, 1996-97 on. Columns: season, nba_gid, gid (ESPN), date, type (RS/PO/PI), team, opp, home, w, pts, opp_pts, margin, coach, opp_coach; neutral, city, alt (m), travel_miles (from the previous game's place), tz_shift, tz_from_home, rest_days, b2b, three_in_four, trip_game, phase (first10/pre_asb/post_asb/last10), game_no; poss, opp_poss, pace, ortg, drtg, efg, tov_pct, orb_pct, ftr, fg3r, ast_pct and the o_ versions allowed; luck (opp 3P/FT points above league rate); pf, o_pf, take_fouls; diet/o_diet (zone -> [share of FGA, FG%]); trans_share, o_trans_share; lead_max, deficit_max, sec_leading, h1_margin, q3_margin, q4_margin, ot, comeback, blown, clutch, garbage, officials, attendance; spread (team view), ou, provider, cover, over; wp_min, wp_max, wp_q4 (ESPN win probability, team view); missing (regular ids out), missing_impact (their BPM), starters, starters_same; opp_net_prior, opp_rank_prior, opp_tier_prior, own_net_prior (prior games only), opp_pace_prior, own_pace_prior, tempo_vs_expected, tempo_toward_own; opp_net_final, opp_playoff; returning_min_share, avg_age, avg_exp.
tables.stints: One row per stint (a stretch with the same ten men), 2002-03 on: both fives (NBA player ids), period, clock at start and end, seconds, possessions, points, the home margin at the start, and each side's 3PM/3PA/FTM/FTA, FGA/FGM, OREB, DREB, TOV.
tables.units: Five- and two-man units per coach-team-season, 2002-03 on: minutes, possessions, games, ratings, net, luck-adjusted net (adj), sample-adjusted net (est, k possessions toward the team), the projection from parts (proj, five-man; pair_adj is the part of it from the lineup pairings that replicated, 2018-19 on), Σ BPM, the quality of opposing fives faced (oppq, Σ BPM), eFG, opponent eFG, ORB%, TOV%.
tables.rotation: One row per player-game for players on the coach's Rotation Map, 2002-03 on: intervals on the floor (seconds from tip-off), off-script minutes by cause (absence, blowout, foul trouble, choice) and scripted minutes.
tables.decisions: One row per event, 2002-03 on: timeouts, challenges, opponent runs (and whether a timeout answered them), fouling up three, two-for-ones, end-of-period possessions, foul-trouble spells. The legend in each file says what a-e hold for each kind.
tables.coaches: Every coach Basketball-Reference lists, 1946-47 on: bio, head-coaching records by season and team, assistant stints, awards, Coach of the Year voting, transactions; the game-level tenures 1996-97 on; staffs by team-season; the acting-coach fixes; the tree.
